intro: A trust is a record per partner Kerberos realm in this realm's directory: the keys this realm holds with it, its attributes ([MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7.9), the DNS suffixes referred to it, and whether it is used. No key or password is ever shown here; a generated key is shown once, when it is made.
noKerberos: This realm has no Kerberos realm of its own (krb5.realm and krb5.enabled), so it holds no trust.
settingsNow: Now: at most {hops} trusts on a referral path; a rotated incoming key accepted for {grace} s; classic delegation across trusts {classic}; SID filtering required in product {filtering}.
productRule: This realm is in product mode: a trust that is not quarantined is not used while krb5.requireSidFilteringInProduct is on.
unknown: This realm holds no trust with {partner}.
addIntro: The partner's administrator records the same trust on their side: the same password (at least {min} characters), or the keys shown once after a generate.
needWrite: Adding, changing, rotating and removing a trust needs Admin Write.
health.disabled: Disabled: it refers nobody and accepts nothing; its keys are kept.
health.unfilteredRefused: Not quarantined, and product mode does not use it while krb5.requireSidFilteringInProduct is on.
health.unfiltered: Not quarantined: product mode will not use it while krb5.requireSidFilteringInProduct is on.
health.incomingHeld: Incoming key held (kvno {kvno}): the partner's tickets are accepted.
health.incomingMissing: No incoming key: no ticket from the partner is accepted.
health.outgoingMissing: No outgoing key: nobody is referred to the partner.
health.unrouted: Routes no DNS suffix: only a realm named outright is referred.
health.paired: Trust realm {realm} holds the matching record.
health.unpaired: Trust realm {realm} holds no record for this realm: Pair writes it.
rotateIntro: New keys at the next kvno. The incoming version it replaces still opens the partner's tickets for {grace} s, until the partner's side changes too.
mirror: Rotate the partner trust realm's record too (a service administrator's act)
removeIntro: Removing a trust takes its keys with it: no referral is made through it and no ticket is accepted from it, at once. Disable keeps the keys.
hForest: Forest trust information (a cross-forest trust only)
forestIntro: The partner forest's domains, one per line: domain SID, DNS name, NetBIOS name, and disabled where its SIDs may not cross; and its top-level names, one per line, with disabled where routing to it is off.
partnerTrustRealm: Trust realm (for a trust realm here)
keysKept: A key already held is kept; Rotate key changes it. The key source is used only for a side the direction adds.
keysOnce: A generated key is shown once, after the trust is added; a password is never shown back.
across.heading: Across trusts
across.intro: What this service's Kerberos delegation means across this realm's trusts. krb5S4uSelfRealm and krb5ForeignTgtDelegation are fields above; the delegation lists stay on Every protocol, under Delegation and Impersonation.
across.hTargets: Foreign targets it may delegate to (appAllowedToDelegateTo)
across.hSelf: Realms whose users it may impersonate (krb5S4uSelfRealm)
across.noFrontEnds: No front end of another realm is named.
across.noTargets: No target of another realm is named.
across.noSelfRealms: No other realm is named: S4U2Self is for this realm's users only.
across.unconstrainedOn: This service is trusted for delegation; krb5ForeignTgtDelegation is {setting}. A user of another realm's TGT reaches it only where the trust allows TGT delegation and the setting is not deny.
across.unconstrainedOff: This service is not trusted for delegation, so no TGT is delegated to it from any realm (krb5ForeignTgtDelegation is {setting}).
across.problem.missing: This realm holds no trust reaching {realm}.
across.problem.notAccepting: The trust with {partner} holds no incoming key, so it accepts nothing.
across.problem.notReferring: The trust with {partner} holds no outgoing key, so nothing is referred there.
across.problem.unfilteredProduct: The trust with {partner} is not quarantined, and product mode does not use it.
across.problem.classicOffHere: Classic delegation across realms is off in this realm (krb5.crossRealmClassicDelegation): it is refused.
across.problem.classicOffThere: Classic delegation across realms is off in {realm}: it is refused there.
